brief: A month ago the Fed's next move hinged on core CPI's second decimal; now the bar is lower. September's FOMC hiked for the first time since July 2023 right after August core CPI hit its lowest since 2021, and minutes showed all 19 officials backing it with most seeing another hike by year-end. Then September payrolls printed a dismal 29K and wage growth slowed to 3.0%, so Jefferson, Williams, Waller and Bowman all turned patient, and October hike odds collapsed from about 70% to about 20% while December stays roughly 72% priced. Wednesday's CPI sets the tone for both meetings: consensus expects a hot 0.6% headline (gasoline) but a tame 0.2% core (shelter offsetting autos and airfares), with Goldman slightly above consensus on core at 0.24%, translating to 0.20% core PCE. Goldman sees core slowing toward 0.1% by year-end, is more dovish than consensus for 2027, but flags upside risk if the oil disruption persists, and FOMC minutes already tie the AI buildout to core goods inflation. Options price SPX for a non-event while FX prices a large move; the piece argues energy keeps feeding CPI and the Fed is not as clear of it as it thinks.
